h: The First Love That Cannot Be Forgotten

p: "'And Tziyon said: Hashem has forsaken me,
and my Lord has forgotten me' (Yeshayahu 49:14):
is not forsaken the same as forgotten?
when a man marries a wife in addition to his first wife,
he still remembers the deeds of the first;
You have forsaken me and forgotten me."
how did Reish Lakish's parable answer
"is not forsaking the same as forgetting?"
דָּרַשׁ בַּגְּמָרָא עַל הַפָּסוּק (שָׁם מט, טו)
"Can a woman forget her nursing child,
lack compassion for the child of her womb?":
Will I forget the burnt offerings of rams
that you offered before Me in the wilderness?"
like "a fire offering" for an olah;
and "compassion for the child of her womb"
And why did it take specifically
the offerings of olah and firstborn?
Shlomo offered a thousand burnt offerings,
that the firstborn were not sanctified in the wilderness;
they did not offer firstborn in the wilderness;
for the animals of the Leviim
that the firstborn were sanctified in the wilderness
that firstborn born in the wilderness
what they offered in the wilderness?
that the main question of the Gemara
is about the change of wording:
that with forsaking the Name Havayah is mentioned,
and with forgetting the Name Adnus is mentioned;
with a doubled expression in different words.
that the main point of what Tziyon said,
the Name Havayah was pronounced explicitly;
the Name as it is written in the Mikdash
mentioning the Name as it is written
which indicates "was, is and will be":
And now it is no longer explicit
to the point that they said in Perek Chelek
that one who pronounces the Name with its letters
has no share in Olam Haba,
for it appears that he does not believe at all.
And this is the meaning of "Hashem has forsaken me":
that He went up to Heaven,
like one who marries a wife in addition to his wife;
although Hashem Yisbarach did not choose,
nevertheless He went up to Heaven,
and is the aspect of faith,
שֶׁעַל כָּל פָּנִים עַל יְדֵי הָאֱמוּנָה
a person can picture to himself
stands over him and sees his deeds
And that is why Reish Lakish used the expression
not remembering the deeds of the first;
who called HaKadosh Baruch Hu Master
"the souls they had made in Charan"
was revealed and recognized in completeness
and accepted the yoke of His kingship,
and there was a complete nation
that recognized His mastery and His kingship;
for this was the main purpose
in the creation of the world,
and this is the meaning of "the deeds of the first."
And to this Hashem Yisbarach answered her,
"Can a woman forget her nursing child?",
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (יִרְמְיָה ב, ב)
along the lines of what is written (Yirmiyahu 2:2):
"I remember for you the kindness of your youth,
your following Me in the wilderness,
what they would do in the wilderness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ג וְעוֹד)
as the Midrash says (Shemos Rabbah 3, and elsewhere):
"How many pregnant women are among them?
How many infants are among them?
did you prepare for the pregnant women?
How many kinds of parched grain and nuts
did you prepare for the infants?" etc.
in the word of Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom,
and this is "the kindness of your youth,"
that they shook loose to follow Me into the wilderness,
in the sense of "a fire offering, a pleasing aroma,"
and the burnt offerings that Yisrael offered in the wilderness.
And in Egypt it is written (Shemos 5:1):
that they may celebrate to Me in the wilderness,"
"Let us go a three days' journey
the main purpose of leaving Egypt.
And to Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom,
"When you take the people out of Egypt,
and although it refers to Matan Torah,
nevertheless the unqualified term "you will serve"
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
And about this HaKadosh Baruch Hu said:
"Will I forget the burnt offerings of rams
that you offered before Me in the wilderness?"
and this is the meaning of "the deeds of the first."
"Compassion for the child of her womb"
this is the sanctification of the firstborn
for they are bound at the root,
and it refers to the main sanctification of the firstborn,
which was at the Exodus from Egypt.
that it is impossible to forget
this is the event at Sinai";
for His mastery and His kingship
they accepted chiefly at Matan Torah,
when they accepted upon themselves the yoke of His kingship
by keeping the entire Torah and the mitzvos.
And then He is called by the name Master,
Who took you out of the land of Egypt":
"Behold, upon the palms I have engraved you";
the form of a man that is on the Throne;
'Let us lift up our hearts to the palms'";
And it refers to the form of
which is engraved on the Throne of Glory;
so how can Tziyon say, "Hashem has forsaken me"?
וְאַף דְּאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (אֵיכָה רַבָּה ב, א)
And although it is found in the Midrash (Eichah Rabbah 2:1)
"He cast down from heaven to earth
כָּךְ אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
"So said HaKadosh Baruch Hu to Yisrael:
only because of the image of Yaakov
that is engraved on My Throne?
"and He did not remember His footstool
on the day of His anger":
that only on the day of His anger
"He cast down from heaven to earth
but when the day of anger passed,
the crown was restored to its former glory,
and the likeness of Yaakov is still engraved
and this is "upon the palms I have engraved you."
And even when He went up to Heaven,
as it were, is upon you.
along the lines of what it says (Pesachim 87a):
these are the synagogues and the study halls."
along the lines of what it says (Yoma 9b)
we will build upon her a turret of silver":
like silver, over which rot has no power,
so that it will endure forever.
And even since the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
HaKadosh Baruch Hu has in His world
אֶלָּא ד׳ אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה בִּלְבַד
only the four cubits of halachah,
in synagogues and in study halls.
And this answers what they said,
that He does not remember the deeds of the first,
that Yisrael are like a wall
against the nations of the world in exile;
and all the troubles that have passed over them
will not succeed in moving them
from the service of Hashem Yisbarach,
as it is expounded in Midrash Shir HaShirim:
when he went down into the furnace."
And this is "Your walls are before Me always":
the yoke of His mastery and His kingship;
